name: Bowness-on-Solway
highlight: Where the wall meets the Solway marshes
description: The western terminus of the wall, and of the modern trail. A quiet coastal village looking out over the Solway Firth to Scotland — flat, open, and a world away from the crags to come.
proof_requirement: Photo at the Hadrian's Wall Path start/finish marker on the village green.

name: Carlisle
highlight: Carlisle Castle, above the Border city
description: The only major city on the route. Roman Luguvalium once stood here, guarding the western crossing — now Carlisle Castle and the Cathedral mark the spot instead.
proof_requirement: Photo at Carlisle Castle or Tullie House.

name: Lanercost Priory
highlight: Built from stone carried off the wall
description: A short detour south of the path. The Augustinian priory was built almost entirely from wall stone taken by the people who came after the Romans — ruin built from ruin.
proof_requirement: Photo at the priory ruins or gatehouse.

name: Birdoswald
highlight: The longest standing stretch on the trail
description: Roman Banna. Home to the longest continuous run of standing wall anywhere on the route, and the clearest place to see the turf-to-stone transition the original builders made.
proof_requirement: Photo on the wall walk immediately east or west of Birdoswald fort.

name: Steel Rigg
highlight: The escarpment, looking north into old frontier country
description: The Whin Sill escarpment — the trail's highest, hardest, and most photographed ground. This is the section most people mean when they picture Hadrian's Wall.
proof_requirement: Photo from the Steel Rigg viewpoint or car park sign.

name: Vindolanda & Housesteads
highlight: Britain's best-preserved fort, and the tablets that gave it a voice
description: Two sites, a couple of miles apart. Housesteads is the best-preserved Roman fort in Britain, sitting right on the path. Vindolanda, just south, is where the wall's most famous find — everyday letters written on wooden tablets — came out of the ground.
proof_requirement: Photo at Housesteads fort, or Vindolanda's excavation site.

name: Chesters Fort
highlight: The best-preserved Roman bathhouse on the wall
description: A cavalry fort on the bank of the North Tyne at Chollerford, with the best-preserved Roman bathhouse anywhere on the route — you can still stand in the rooms where soldiers washed off eighteen centuries ago.
proof_requirement: Photo at the bathhouse ruins by the river.

name: Segedunum
highlight: The viewing tower where the wall meets the Tyne
description: The eastern terminus, at Wallsend. Climb the viewing tower and look down on the excavated fort exactly where the wall met the Tyne and the wild frontier gave way to open sea.
proof_requirement: Photo from the Segedunum viewing tower.
